issues.title: Reduce bundle size
issues.body:
The webpack build process warns our distributable files are too large.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/132400292-3faf6e37-87ae-4ce4-bfb3-252f1c41853b.png)

Most usage of Serge is on a LAN, but even on Heroku it seems to load quickly enough.  Well, at least I think it does - I've always thought the initial delay was the Heroku instance spinning up.

Can we tidily reduce the size of the packages by splitting them up?  At least (I guess) they'll be downloaded in parallel.

We could probably also split up the distribution.  We don't need to deliver `admin` _and_ `player` to the client browser.  In lots of cases the huge `mapping` components aren't required.

With the above exercise, we could also ditch some unused code/components.  `RLI Status Board` is certainly one instance of this, but there are probably old `client` modules, too.

issues.title: Move back to monolith
issues.body:
Early in the project lifetime we moved from a monolith to a mono-repo

But, except for the (very-small) server-side component it really is just one app.    It is also built, distributed, and run as one app.

We should consider returning to a monolith repo.

### Pros
- It would avoid the multiple version numbers spread across the repo
- simpler build process
- simpler architecture

### Cons
- could be a lot of effort
- we will lose ability to run `build` on just one component (`helpers` rebuilds really quickly)
